title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1965 manuscript 'Théorie de Galois des motifs'. Grothendieck develops what became the Tannakian formalism. He has a category T of motives over a ground field k with rational coefficients, viewed as a gerbe or tensor category with a family of 'fibre functors' attached to points x. The page uses two of them: xi_{x,infty}, an 'infinite-place' or Betti-type fibre functor, and xi_{xbar,ell}, the ell-adic one, which takes values in Z_ell-modules. The two neighbouring pages are unrelated Bourbaki typescripts, so the local context is only this page.

Case analysis, continuing from cases i)-iii) on earlier pages:
(1) For different points or base fields, two fibre functors need not be isomorphic. This is the general non-neutral situation, already met in case iii).
(2) One no longer has an action of pi_1(X, .) on xi_{x,infty}. Instead, as in case iii), automorphisms of k over k(x) act on xi_{x,infty} through the descent data (trivialisations). Those inducing the identity on k determine a Q-form of the functor.
(3) Interesting case k = Q. Here xi_{x,infty} is an object of T_x(Q), i.e. a trivialisation (neutralisation) of the gerbe T_Q by a fibre functor with values over Q.
(4) Different such trivialisations are in general not isomorphic a priori. Moreover there is no privileged canonical isomorphism between xi_{x,infty} tensor_Q Q_ell and xi_{xbar,ell} tensor_{Z_ell} Q_ell. His reason: the former comes only from an object of T(Q_ell), not from T(Z_ell), so there is no reason to expect such an isomorphism.
(5) Conclusion: X (or the motive category) over Q defines a cohomology class in H^2(Q_ell, G_ell^{(x)}), i.e. a nonabelian (Giraud) H^2 class measuring the obstruction to comparing the gerbes or neutralisations over Q_ell. In the general case Q_ell must be replaced by something else (the page breaks off).

Margin note: 'en effet, il serait défini sur un groupe sur les motifs de poids et niveau 0'. This suggests that for weight-0, level-0 (Artin) motives a comparison would exist, since there everything is defined via finite Galois sets.

Problem served: understanding how the various realisations or fibre functors of a non-neutral Tannakian category of motives relate. This means torsors of isomorphisms between fibre functors (Isom-torsors under the motivic Galois group) and gerbe classes in nonabelian H^2.
errors: Tension with Artin's comparison theorem. If xi_{x,infty} is the Betti realisation for a complex (or real) point, then the comparison theorem gives a canonical isomorphism Betti tensor Q_ell = ell-adic tensor Q_ell, for motives over a field embedded in C. Grothendieck's denial of a canonical isomorphism must therefore mean that xi_{x,infty} is not the classical Betti functor, or that he means isomorphism of the gerbe-theoretic data compatible with descent. Otherwise the remark is mistaken.

There is a slip between H^1 and H^2. The class of the torsor Isom(omega_1, omega_2) lives in H^1, while the gerbe class lives in H^2. Passing to 'a class in H^2(Q_ell, G_ell)' is asserted without argument.
The transcription is too uncertain in places to pin down 'cas iii)' and the exact role of k(x).

ideas.what: Motive categories as gerbes or tensor categories whose fibre functors at different points or fields are non-isomorphic; trivialisations as fibre functors over Q
ideas.modern_name: Non-neutral Tannakian categories; neutralisation by a fibre functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (ideas, 1960s), written up by Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne-Milne (1982), Deligne (1990)
ideas.where_published: Ideas transmitted via Saavedra's thesis; mentioned in Récoltes et Semailles; not in EGA/SGA

ideas.what: Galois automorphisms of the base acting on fibre functors via descent data
ideas.modern_name: Descent of fibre functors; Galois action on the torsor of fibre functors

ideas.what: Obstruction to comparing Betti-type and ell-adic fibre functors over Q_ell, as a class in nonabelian H^2(Q_ell, G_ell)
ideas.modern_name: Gerbe class of a Tannakian category / comparison torsors in nonabelian cohomology (Giraud)

ideas.what: Weight-0, level-0 (Artin) motives admit the comparison
ideas.modern_name: Artin motives correspond to finite Galois sets

missed.claim: Grothendieck suggests that for motives over Q there need be no privileged isomorphism between the 'infinite' fibre functor tensored with Q_ell and the ell-adic one. The mismatch would give an invariant in H^2(Q_ell, G_ell), with a generalisation for other base fields left unwritten. This is an early version of studying comparison torsors between realisations at a level finer than Artin's comparison theorem.
missed.quote: Ainsi, X [?] sur Q définit une classe de coh. dans H^2(Q_ell, G_ell^{(x)}). Dans le cas général, il faut remplacer Q_ell
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that in 1965 Grothendieck already considered nonabelian H^2 obstructions attached to realisations of motives. Mathematically it is either superseded by Artin's comparison theorem or by later work on period torsors and comparison torsors.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early (1965) sketch of non-neutral Tannakian and gerbe phenomena for motives, which is historically interesting. But the ideas are generally credited to Grothendieck via Saavedra, and the specific H^2 claim is vague and possibly at odds with Artin's comparison theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'perdu[?]' at the start may be 'perdu' or 'prévu'; this is unclear.
'il est dans T_Q un [?] [?] en général pas isomorphes' plausibly reads 'il y a dans T_Q, ne sont en général pas isomorphes'.
'xi_{x,infty} subset T_x(Q)' is better read as 'xi_{x,infty} in T_x(Q)' (an object, not an inclusion).
In the margin, 'défini sur un groupe' may be 'défini sur un groupe' or 'défini a priori'; the phrase 'motifs de poids et niveau 0' is clear.
